thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: spike in 5xx and gateway timeouts for /v1/generate (12:41 UTC) in ap-southeast. Error rate ~14% over 3m window.
sre-oncall: Paging Carl H (primary).
Carl H: On it. Any deploys or traffic shifts?
Maya R: No deploys. Telemetry shows sudden increase in prefix-cache invalidations and a matching rise in retries to kv-store. Heap pressure and GC events on kv-sidecars starting ~12:36.
Nina V: Gateway logs show checksum failures from prefix cache reads and then downstream 502s. Sample logs:
```
[12:36:59] ERROR prefix_cache.go: checksum-failed key=/prefix/ctx/0x9f4 shard=21
[12:37:03] WARN prefix_cache.go: rapid-evict rate=970/s node=kv-proxy-21
[12:37:10] ERROR gateway.go: upstream 504 timeout model-router-2 (ctx=long-context)
```
Support Bot: Incoming tickets: #9110 (media startup) reporting repeated 502s, #9113 (banking partner) seeing timeouts.
Carl H: Hypothesis: a compaction or background maintenance created partial writes -> checksum mismatch on cached blocks -> cache returns invalid blobs -> callers retry -> thundering retries -> backend saturation -> 5xx/timeouts.
Maya R: I can confirm a compaction job ran at 12:34 on shard 21 and 27. CRC-mismatch count jumped at 12:35.
Nina V: Immediate mitigation idea: disable prefix-cache reads for affected shards (read-through) and enable cache checksum-failure fast-fail to prevent retries. Can we flip quickly?
Carl H: Yes. There's a config toggle `prefix.cache.mode=read-through` that can be applied per-route via runtime config. I'll push a canary change to ap-southeast gateways targeting routes with long-context models.
incident-bot: Runbook step created RB#2061: apply routing override + start kv-verify job.
Maya R: Starting live kv-verify for shard=21 in verify-only mode. Do not repair yet.
Carl H: Canary applied to 4 hosts now (gw-211, gw-214, gw-220, gw-227). Monitoring.
Nina V: Observed canary results: those hosts 5xx dropped from 13.5% -> 0.6% within 60s. Overall region error-rate reduced to ~2.1%. Latency increased ~18ms for those flows.
Support Bot: Notifying affected customers: posting interim update: "We're investigating an elevated error rate affecting some API calls. A temporary mitigation is active; we're validating data integrity. Next update in 30m."
Maya R: kv-verify results: shard 21 -> 34 keys flagged CRC mismatch; shard 27 -> 9 keys. Most keys are adjacent in keyspace near compaction boundary. Exporting suspect key list now.
Carl H: Good. Next: drain hosts still serving cached reads, promote canary to 25% gradually, and add a circuit-breaker on prefix-cache path to auto-fail to read-through when checksum-errors > 3% over 1m.
Nina V: I pushed the circuit-breaker rule to feature flags; should auto-flip for unhealthy shards.
Maya R: Preparing snapshot of flagged keys and copying to forensic bucket for deeper analysis. Will not run repair without snapshot.
incident-bot: Pager update: severity reduced to SEV3 at 12:52 UTC due to mitigation effectiveness.
Carl H: We should also add a temporary retry-budget to client-facing routes to limit amplification while we heal. Implementing short lived limit now.
Support Bot: Delivered customer update: "Mitigation reduced errors significantly; engineers are continuing verification. Estimated time to full remediation: 90 minutes."
Maya R: Action items being tracked: 1) Forensic export of suspect keys 2) Add compaction-smoke tests for checksum invariants 3) Implement per-shard auto-failover to read-through 4) Plan maintenance window for safe repair (low-traffic window) 5) Postmortem owner assignment.
Carl H: I'll own the repair runbook and automation. Nina + Maya will co-author postmortem. Liaise with Support for final customer timeline.
Nina V: Adding note: we observed retry amplification in gateway logs due to clients retrying on 502s; we should consider a global short-term client retry-suppression feature during incidents.
Maya R: Export complete. Snapshot size: 2.1MB. Uploaded to s3://incidents/4932100001/forensics.tar.gz
Carl H: Rolling canary to 25% now. Hosts showing stable 5xx <1%. Ready to promote more if stable.
incident-bot: Incident handoff: live mitigation channel will be closed at 13:00 UTC and oncall will continue watch.
Nina V: We'll hold off on repair until the low-traffic window at 03:00 UTC and prepare a safe-apply plan with smoke tests to re-enable cache gradually.
Support Bot: CS notified customers of maintenance window and provided PTR for updates.
Carl H: Closing live incident thread. Postmortem meeting scheduled 11:00 UTC tomorrow. Summary: compaction edge produced checksum mismatches -> prefix-cache returned invalid payloads -> retry amplification -> gateway timeouts/5xx. Mitigations: read-through routing, circuit-breaker, retry-budgets, forensic export.
Nina V: Thanks team. :shipit:
